message.content: Logistic regression is a statistical method used for predicting the probability of a binary outcome (e.g., success/failure, yes/no) based on one or more predictor variables. It models the relationship between the predictors and the log‑odds of the outcome using a linear combination of the predictors, then applies the logistic (sigmoid) function to map the result to a probability between 0 and 1. The model parameters are typically estimated via maximum likelihood estimation, and the fitted model can be used for classification or to interpret the influence of each predictor on the outcome.
